subject: Climate & Environment
title: Flash Floods
description: Learn Flash Floods in one minute.

hook.text: A flash flood can turn a dry creek bed into a raging river in under an hour.

buildup.text: Intense rainfall overwhelms the ground's ability to absorb water. The excess runs off instantly.

discovery.text: Urban areas flood fastest — concrete and asphalt prevent any water from soaking in.

twist.text: Just 15 centimeters of fast-moving water can knock an adult off their feet.

climax.text: Half of all flood deaths occur in vehicles. People underestimate the power of moving water.

punchline.text: Water is gentle until it moves. Then nothing stands in its way.

quiz.question: Why do urban areas flood more easily than rural ones?
options: Concrete and asphalt prevent water absorption
Buildings block wind that would dry rain
Cities get more rainfall than rural areas

details.summary: Flash floods occur when intense rainfall overwhelms drainage capacity within minutes to hours, turning dry streambeds into torrents. They kill more people than any other flood type because they develop too fast for warnings to reach all at-risk populations.
details.whyItMatters: Climate change is intensifying rainfall rates, increasing flash flood risk. Urbanization adds impermeable surfaces that convert rain to runoff instantly.
takeaways: Flash floods can develop within minutes of intense rainfall
Urbanization dramatically increases flash flood risk
Just 15 centimeters of moving water can knock a person down

faq.question: Why are flash floods so deadly?
faq.answer: They develop faster than warnings can be issued and reach full force within minutes. People are often caught in vehicles, basements, or low-lying areas with no escape route. The force of fast-moving water sweeps away cars and destroys buildings.

faq.question: How does urbanization increase flash flood risk?
faq.answer: Pavement, rooftops, and compacted soil prevent rainwater from soaking in. In natural landscapes, soil absorbs much of the rain. In cities, nearly all rain becomes immediate surface runoff, overwhelming drainage systems designed for lighter storms.
